messages:
support-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (hosted inference) starting 1871234490. P50 latency up 3x. Customers reporting timeouts. Auto-escalating to #incidents 

samir: seeing it too, confirmed spike in 5xx from canary pool A. rolling window shows errors jump at 1871234488. :eyes:

elaine: any recent deploys?

rohan: yes, canary rollout 2026-11-02T14:21:00 UTC for feature 'dynamic-routing-v2' and flip of flag `route_by_latency` landed 14:20.

maureen: hold — support getting panicked customers (TS-9812, TS-9813) with timeouts + occasional 502 gateway. They also reported billing shows duplicate tokens consumed for some requests.

samir: logs show backend returns 500 with message `kv-cache: incompatible shard` and `rpc: stream ended`. Here's a sample: ```ERROR inference/proxy.go:412: upstream error: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
2026-11-02T14:20:30Z request_id=abc123 model=redwood-13b-v2 shard=canary-A
```

jem: reproducer from curl (from eu-west region): ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate``` returns 502 with body `\{"error":"gateway: upstream closed"\}` consistently for canary routing.

ops-oncall: rolling through metrics now. P95 latency for canary-A nodes > 2.5s, heavy retry churn. Non-canary pools stable.

elaine: seems like flag flip routed more traffic to canary-A which is a mixed-quantized variant. Could be a mismatch between proxy routing behavior and runtime kernels.

rohan: checking rollout config: the canary was supposed to get 5% but due to a routing policy bug it got 35% (flag `canary_percent` accidentally set to 35 in feature-release). I see an automated deploy script patch earlier today: `deploy patch --set canary_percent=35`.

maureen: oh wow. Did the script run as a part of CI? Who signed off?

samir: it was an ops convenience script; owner tag is @rohan. Noticed in logs: heavy connection resets from quantized backend processes.

jem: customers: some also reported 401s intermittently — probably retries hitting a different auth cluster. Support stack is noisy.

ops-oncall: plan: immediately reduce traffic to canary-A, disable `route_by_latency` feature flag, and if stable, rollback canary build to previous image.

rohan: issuing command now: ```rdeploy set-traffic --service=inference-api --pool=canary-A --percent=0 --reason="hotfix-5xx-spike"```

deploy-bot: deployment event: set-traffic succeeded. canary-A traffic -> 0% at 1871234560 by rohan.

samir: traffic drop confirmed. 5xx rate dropped ~80% in 2 min. P95 latency back to baseline on gateway. :thumbsup:

elaine: leave canary isolated and collect heap + debug logs. Do not fully shut down until we confirm root cause.

maureen: support: telling customers we are mitigating and will follow up within 60m. Documenting impacted requests and issuing refunds for double-billed tokens if found.

rohan: capturing core dumps and runtime logs. Early hypothesis: a config flag in runtime `enable_kv_cache_shard` default mismatch between proxy and runtime images causing aborts under load.

samir: found a golden example in logs: `panic: kv cache shard mismatch: expected 16, got 8` followed by goroutine shutdown. That aligns with incompatible binary versions.

jem: can we map which commit/tag landed in canary-A? rohan: it's `inference-runtime:v3.7.0-canary` which included a new shard-count default.

ops-oncall: escalation path: we should rollback runtime image on canary-stable nodes and re-deploy compatible build to canary-A. MAUREEN, can you coordinate customer comms?

maureen: on it. Sending update to affected customers. Also opening billing ticket to auto-refund any duplicate charges. Ticket: BILL-4491.

rohan: next step: revert canary image to `inference-runtime:v3.6.9` and re-enable routing after tests. Rolling now: ```rdeploy image-update --pool=canary-A --image=inference-runtime:v3.6.9 --force```

deploy-bot: image-update started (task id rtask-9842). Expected ~3m per node.

samir: adding a temporary middleware to catch `kv-cache` errors and return 503 with explanatory body to avoid confusing upstream billing receipts. Will push patch to proxy: ```git revert -m 1 aa12bc3 && make build && deploy proxy-canary```

elaine: after rollback completes, we should add a preflight check to the deployment pipeline: verify `kv_shard_count` is identical across proxy and runtime or block the rollout.

jem: keeping an eye on auth anomalies — once traffic normalizes we'll triage 401 chatter separately.

ops-oncall: image-update finished at 1871234875. All nodes back to v3.6.9. No new 5xxs observed in 5m window.

samir: confirming: 5xx rate baseline restored. Closing immediate incident but leaving thread open for follow-ups (postmortem, pipeline guard, billing refunds).

maureen: status update sent to customers at 1871234900. Will follow up with credits list for BILL-4491.

rohan: filing a rollback runbook PR with explicit gating checks. Also will revert the `canary_percent` CI script to avoid accidental large canary flips.

jem: happy path restored. Thanks everyone for quick response. :heart:

support-bot: RESOLVED(?): monitor for 60m and escalate if 5xx > 0.5%

samir: adding assigned owners for postmortem: samir, rohan, elaine, maureen, jem. I'll kick off a postmortem doc.
